originality.rationale: No inspected published claim implies the exact all-window quartic norm or thirteen-point maximum. The closest exact sharp all-window result is for degree two/three, and it explicitly excludes higher polynomial degrees. Degree-four kernels have two sign changes on a half-window, unlike that prior case. Original filter coefficients and the generic convolution-norm identity are not asserted as original; unindexed historical equivalents remain possible.
residual_risks: An older unindexed equivalent computation of the quartic full family may exist, especially described as filter negativity or ℓ1 impulse-response gain.
Original 1964 article full PDF was publisher-restricted and not fully inspected; public coefficients themselves are prior art.

value.rationale: A natural fixed-degree family-wide robustness invariant is resolved completely: thirteen points uniquely maximize total variation under quartic local polynomial smoothing; the long-window limit differs strictly. This is not a free finite slice or merely reproducing a coefficient table; it supplies a global optimum with an independent infinite-tail proof and informs worst-case filter selection.
